title: What is big data?
section: My rant: We should think more about models and less about data
text:
My rant: We should think more about models and less about data
We are going to be talking a lot about data in this module.
We should never lose sight of the social science question behind our analysis.
IMO (you may disagree) data are there to inform model parameters – the model (that is – the thing you want to find out) is always more important than the data.


McElreath, R. (2020). Statistical rethinking: A Bayesian course with examples in R and Stan (2e ed.). CRC press Boca Raton, FL.

title: What is big data?
section: Big data as the 3 or maybe 6 V’s
text:
Big data as the 3 or maybe 6 V’s

Volume (it’s big)
Velocity (updated frequently)
Variety (heterogeneous)
Validity (probably not much?)
Veracity (correctness and accuracy – it depends?)
Volatility (very!)

title: What is big data?
text:
Primary data
Advantages

Ability to use precisely the questions we want
Complete freedom over how constructed
(Relative) control over sample size and can identify under-represented groups

Disadvantages

Time-consuming to get access to data
Need to construct the actual questionnaire
Access to the perfect sample might not be possible

title: What is big data?
text:
Secondary data
Advantages

Availability
Quality controlled?
Usually comes with some measures of representation, including survey weights

Disadvantages

Analyses can become variable-driven
Can only analyse what’s there
Little idea about response rates or why some (or lots) of data is missing

title: What is big data?
text:
By-product data

Data which exists ‘naturally’ that we want to use for research purposes
Administrative data
NHS records, linked tax records, school exam results
Social media data
Tweets, Facebook posts, Instagram posts?
Online metadata
Internet Movie Database (IMDB) information about films

Advantages

Enables us to access ‘hard-to-reach’ data
Cost-effective way of gathering huge amounts of data

title: What is big data?
text:
By-product data
As with Primary Data

Time-consuming to get access to data
Lots of data cleaning/labelling required
Access to the perfect sample might not be possible

As with Secondary Data

Analysis can become variable-driven
Limited to only having data on the information available
Variables often have limited sophistication
Little idea about who isn’t included or why data is missing

title: What is big data?
text:
By-product data limitations

‘Comprehensive’ data is rarely comprehensive
People not registered with NHS?
X/Twitter feed data will exclude deleted tweets
We are given ‘found’ data as it is found
Useful social science data is rarely included
Often unusual practices in what is preserved

title: What is big data?
text:
By-product data limitations (continued)

Little contextualisation to the data
People might have died five years ago
Tweets might include irony, or be about a different subject (#BSA)
Would text-based analysis work for TikTok?

title: What is big data?
text:
Working with by-product data

Ethnicity selection amongst online daters
200m messages from 9m users of large US dating website (2003-2010 data)
Studied focused on 6.7m initial messages, with 8.5% receiving a reply
Study found that people with a ‘multiracial’ identity were more likely to receive a response

title: What is big data?
text:
Working with by-product data

Data accessed through a formal contract with the website
High quality quantitative data, but required detailed negotiations
Able to identify attitudes towards dating people from different ethnic groups

title: What is big data?
section: Types of big data: Administrative data
text:
Types of big data: Administrative data

Data from government departments made available to researchers
Research institutes can link datasets through shared IDs or probabilistically
Nice in theory, but tricky in practice

title: What is big data?
section: Types of big data: social media/web data
text:
Types of big data: social media/web data

From social media sites through APIs
Or ‘digital trace’ data scraped from the web
Does analysis of social media represent empirical or methodological social science?
Much analysis focuses on platform behaviour rather than wider society

title: What is big data?
text:
In summary

We can think of big data as having the three (or six) V’s
As being by-product data
It shares some features (mostly limitations) with traditional primary and secondary data
